entities.name: Josceline de Bohon
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Josceline de Bohon (died 25 November 1184) was a prominent Anglo-Norman cleric who served as Bishop of Salisbury from 1142 until his resignation in 1184. His episcopacy spanned a tumultuous period in English history, encompassing the anarchy of King Stephen's reign and the contentious early years of Henry II's rule, during which he became a key figure in the Becket controversy and the broader struggle between ecclesiastical and royal power. His family, the Bohuns, were significant landowners, enhancing his influence within the realm.

Appointed Bishop of Salisbury by King Stephen, Josceline quickly became entangled in the political and religious conflicts of the era. He participated in the Council of Reims in 1148 and, more notably, was a staunch supporter of King Henry II during the Becket controversy. He was present at the Council of Clarendon in 1164, where the Constitutions of Clarendon, which sought to limit the jurisdiction of ecclesiastical courts, were promulgated. For his continued loyalty to the king, Josceline, along with other bishops, was excommunicated by Thomas Becket in 1169, a sentence later lifted by papal legates. He consecrated Richard of Ilchester as Bishop of Winchester in 1174, further demonstrating his role within the English hierarchy.

Josceline's long tenure as Bishop of Salisbury, lasting over four decades, solidified the diocese's administrative and spiritual foundations amidst significant political upheaval. His consistent alignment with royal authority, particularly during the Becket dispute, underscored the deep divisions within the English Church regarding its relationship with the crown and contributed to the ongoing debate about the prerogatives of secular versus spiritual power. His actions helped define the boundaries of episcopal loyalty in an age of competing fealties, influencing how future bishops navigated similar conflicts.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Josceline de Bohon was a long-serving Bishop of Salisbury whose unwavering support for Henry II during the Becket controversy significantly impacted the balance of power between the English Crown and the Church in the 12th century, illustrating the profound challenges of episcopal loyalty.
